verses.text: A psalm by Asaph. God, the nations have invaded what belongs to you. They’ve defiled your holy temple and left Jerusalem in piles of rubble.
They’ve left your servants’ bodies for the birds to eat and the flesh of your faithful people for wild animals.
They’ve poured out blood like water all around Jerusalem. Nobody was left to bury the dead.
We’ve become a disgrace to our neighbors. Everyone around us laughs and mocks us.
How long, LORD? Will you stay angry forever? Will your jealousy keep burning like fire?
Pour out your wrath on nations that don’t know you and kingdoms that never call on your name.
They’ve devoured Jacob and wrecked his homeland.
Don’t hold our ancestors’ wrongs against us. Let your tender mercy reach us quickly. We’re desperate.
Help us, God who saves us, for the glory of your name. Rescue us and forgive our sins for the sake of your name.
Why should the nations get to say, “Where’s their God?” Let them see, right in front of us, that you’re avenging your servants’ blood.
Let the prisoners’ groans reach you. Use your great power to save those sentenced to die.
Lord, pay our neighbors back seven times over for the insults they threw at you.
Then we, your people, the sheep of your pasture, will thank you forever. We’ll tell every generation why you deserve praise.
